name: Kripasamudra Perumal Temple, Thirusirupuliyur
deity: Vishnu as Kripasamudra (Arulmakadal, Sthalasayana) Perumal, reclining, with the Goddess Thirumamagal Nachiyar
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thirusirupuliyur, Vishnu reclines in a small form as Kripasamudra, the ocean of grace, shown to the sage Vyaghrapada — a Divya Desam of Chola Nadu sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thirusirupuliyur lies in the Nannilam taluk of the Tiruvarur district, about two kilometres from Kollumangudi. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Chola Nadu, where Thirumangai Alvar offered his hymns to the Lord. The temple is known by several names: Kripasamudra, meaning ocean of grace, Arulmakadal in Tamil, and Sthalasayana Perumal for the Lord who reclines on the ground. Dated inscriptions and a firm building history are not recorded in the sources we have, so the shrine is honoured chiefly through the Alvar's hymns.
sections.architecture: A four-tiered rajagopuram stands at the entrance, and the sanctum is crowned by the Nanda Vardhana Vimanam. The sthala vriksham is the vilvam tree. Within the sanctum the Lord reclines in a small form, in the posture called Bala Sayanam, and faces south, with the Goddess Thirumamagal Nachiyar beside him. Images of the sages Vyaghrapada and Kanva are also in the sanctum.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Vyaghrapada, the tiger-footed, who worshipped here. As the aged sages could not take in a vast form, the Lord showed himself in a small reclining form, and the place took its name from siru, small, puli, tiger, and ur, place. Tradition adds that the Lord here gave refuge to Adisesha from Garuda. Another tradition says that Thirumangai Alvar remarked on how small the image was, and was told to see the Lord in his larger form at Thirukkannamangai.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps three daily rituals and three yearly festivals in the Vaishnava tradition; the festival calendar is not recorded in detail in the sources we have, so confirm dates locally. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the days of the Alvars are customarily honoured at Divya Desams of the Chola country.
sections.experience: A small, quiet shrine where the lesson is in its scale: the Lord who is an ocean of grace appears as a modest reclining form. Pilgrims tracing Thirumangai Alvar's hymns often pair it with Thirukkannamangai, as the tradition suggests. Visit in daylight, take time over the images of Vyaghrapada and Kanva, and confirm timings locally.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirusirupuliyur is about two kilometres from Kollumangudi in the Tiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu, about 17 kilometres from Mayiladuthurai and about 10 kilometres from Karaikal. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest large railhead, and Tiruchirappalli is the nearest major airport. Reach it by road, and confirm local directions on arrival.
